attrs.definition: A model-based RL architecture in which (1) all components learn continually, (2) each weight has a meta-learned step-size (online cross-validation), and (3) state+time abstractions are continually created via the FC-STOMP progression; a design-general, experiential, open-ended path to superintelligence.

Feature Construction -> pose a SubTask on a feature -> learn an Option solving it -> learn a Model of the option -> Plan with the model. The five-step loop by which OaK builds temporal abstractions grounded in experience.

The agent is orders of magnitude smaller than its environment; it can neither fully perceive world-state nor represent optimal action everywhere, so it must approximate, selectively remember/forget, and continually adapt. Computationally efficient/approximate methods win in big worlds.
All of what we mean by goals and purposes can be well thought of as maximization of expected cumulative scalar reward.
Learn one step at a time from a non-stationary experience stream without storing or replaying data; the frozen train-then-deploy paradigm is rejected.
Standard deep nets progressively lose the ability to learn under continual training; preserving plasticity (e.g. continual backprop injecting variability) is a prerequisite for lifelong learning.
Each parameter learns its own step-size by meta-gradient / online cross-validation rather than sharing a uniform learning rate — enabling fast, robust credit assignment on noisy streams.

Options = (policy pi, termination gamma) as temporally-extended actions; General Value Functions represent predictive knowledge. Temporal abstraction in planning is the historically under-used half of abstraction OaK targets.
Agents acquire superhuman ability predominantly from their own streams of experience (interaction + grounded reward), moving beyond the 'era of human data' / imitation of human text.
Over 70 years, general methods that leverage computation (search + learning) beat methods that build in human knowledge; the latter plateau. Directs OaK away from hand-engineered domain knowledge.

attrs.definition: A cross-field (AI, psychology, economics, control, neuroscience) skeleton of a decision-maker: input/output/goal + perception, decision, value, and world-model components — with no domain-specific content.

Pairing event-driven neural networks with batch-size-one learning for orders-of-magnitude less compute/energy; 'holy grail' target = a trillion-parameter agent learning+planning in real time on ~20W (human-brain budget).

entities.name: Superintelligence can and should arise from an agent's own run-time experience (continual learning), not from design-time human engineering: 'We want AI agents that can discover like we can, not which contain what we have discovered.'

AGI requires model-based RL that plans with a world model abstract in BOTH state and time; temporal abstraction (options) is the historically missing piece, and options must be discovered so their models are useful for planning.

In realistic problems the agent is orders of magnitude smaller than the world; therefore it must use computationally efficient approximation, selective memory, and perpetual online adaptation — a permanent condition, not a temporary hardware limit.
Reward maximization is by itself sufficient to underpin all intelligence (natural and artificial) and provides a suitable basis for AGI.
A single scalar reward is NOT sufficient; capturing intelligence needs multi-objective / vector-valued rewards. (Direct rebuttal of 'Reward is Enough'.)

LLMs are a dead end for AGI: they model 'what a human would say next,' not a true action-conditioned world model; they lack a goal and cannot learn on the job. Experiential learners will supersede them (another instance of the Bitter Lesson).

COUNTER (Dwarkesh): pretrained LLMs can serve as a convenient, plentiful prior/intermediary on which experiential learning is layered — non-renewable does not mean dead-end (the 'fossil fuels' analogy).
A new generation of agents will acquire superhuman capabilities by learning predominantly from their own experience streams, ending the 'era of human data.'

Standard deep learning loses plasticity under continual learning until it learns no better than a shallow net; sustained lifelong learning requires a continual, partly-random source of variability (e.g. continual backprop). This is a precondition for OaK's 'all components learn continually.'
Fast, robust learning on noisy streams needs per-weight meta-learned step-sizes (IDBD / online cross-validation) rather than uniform credit assignment.

The endgame is a trillion-parameter agent that learns and plans in real time on ~20W via event-driven nets + batch-size-one learning — using orders of magnitude less compute/energy than current methods.
General methods that leverage computation (search + learning) ultimately beat human-knowledge-engineered methods by a large margin.

RL rests on three questionable 'dogmas' (environment as a single stationary MDP-like object, reward as an adequate scalar signal, and an evaluation-first stance); rethinking them is needed for continual, big-world agents.

attrs.scope: What general/foundation intelligence requires (continual learning, memory, long-horizon agency, world models, reliability/verification, self-improvement) and the methodologies pursued toward it.

attrs.definition: Agent iteratively rewrites its own code/harness (outer loop) while an inner loop optimizes against evaluations; open-ended archive-based variants echo Darwinian evolution.
Population/archive-based mutation + selection over prompts, harnesses, code artifacts (Pareto/Elo/quality-diversity) to discover better agent scaffolds without gradient training.
Chain-of-thought, test-time compute, planning/search at inference to raise reliability on novel/long tasks. (Stub here; deep-populate in D5 Reasoning.)
Ordering of evaluators (formal verifier > process-reward model > rubric > intrinsic self-assessment); demonstrated self-improvement strength tracks the verifier's position in this hierarchy.
Learning new things at deployment without catastrophic forgetting; persistent memory/skill stores across long streams. Frontier finding: bolt-on memory scaffolds can HURT long-horizon reliability.
Predict future in an abstract latent representation rather than reconstructing pixels/tokens; enables planning, physical reasoning, sim2real. LeCun's JEPA family is the flagship.

Theory-grounded JEPA: isotropic-Gaussian optimal embedding + Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization (SIGReg); heuristics-free, ~50 LoC; ViT-H/14 reaches 79% ImageNet linear.

AGI ~2030 (±1yr) but current paradigm has ~50/50 odds of missing 1–2 big ideas; the unsolved gaps are continual learning, robust memory, world physics/models, consistency, and introspective reasoning — 'scale is all you need' is incomplete.

'Powerful AI' (smarter than Nobel laureates across most fields) could arrive as early as 2027; interpretability is urgent; world models + continual learning are needed if self-improvement doesn't deliver on its own.

Large-scale pretraining / LLMs are a 'dead end' for superintelligence; true AI needs agents that learn continually from experience at runtime (OaK: options + world-model knowledge from raw experience).

Autoregressive LLMs won't reach general intelligence on their own; intelligence needs systems that model the world, simulate outcomes, and plan — JEPA (latent prediction) over token/pixel reconstruction.

'Decade of agents', not year; still missing continual learning, long-term memory, reliable tool use — a ~10-year grind. 'Cognitive core': strip memory so the model looks things up, keeping only algorithms for thought. LLMs show jagged intelligence + anterograde amnesia.

Fluid intelligence (efficiently acquiring new skills / solving novel problems from minimal examples) is the missing piece for general AI; ARC-AGI-2 isolates it — frontier ~75–85 vs human ~66, ARC-AGI-3 <1%.
The next era: agents inhabit continuous lifelong streams of experience with grounded sensor-motor actions and rewards and non-human reasoning; experiential data will eclipse human data.
Bolt-on memory scaffolds UNIVERSALLY hurt long-horizon performance across all 10 tested models (23,392 episodes); reliability ≠ capability.
Naive in-context learning beats dedicated memory systems on continual-learning streams; naive streams can't even distinguish memory designs.
Memory helps IF the agent learns to USE it (not merely store): a 9B model with learned memory-use challenges a 397B model.
A Continuum Memory System with multi-frequency modules (HOPE, self-modifying Titans) mitigates catastrophic forgetting and beats Titans/Samba/Transformers on long-context + reasoning.
Demonstrated self-improvement strength TRACKS the verification hierarchy (formal > PRM > rubric > intrinsic); a scaffold with a weak/intrinsic verifier can lose to a plain checklist.

73.8% of Kernel-Bench and 46.8% of ALE-Bench 'optimizations' in self-improving code agents were proxy gains without real gains; models know they're reward hacking and telling them to stop can make it worse.
A biased internal judge silently disables skill retirement; false-pass bias past a sharp threshold is unrecoverable by any amount of data, and the damage surfaces in NO aggregate metric.
GEPA (reflective Pareto prompt evolution) can outperform reinforcement learning and tops evolutionary baselines with `optimize_anything`.

On Terminal-Bench 2.0 continual eval, GEPA's optimized agent transfers BELOW the unoptimized baseline; RELAI-VCL is the only optimizer that transfers positively and keeps improving (76.4% vs 66.0% GEPA lifelong). Gains compound only when regression control is built into the loop.
On a defective seed, GEPA DEGRADES accuracy (GSM8K 23.81%→13.50%); VISTA recovers to 87.57% by decoupling hypothesis-gen from rewrite + explore/exploit.
Harness-only changes (no model swap) moved a coding agent 52.8%→66.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 (rank ~30→top-5): scaffolding compounds on a capable model.
Automatic harness evolution does NOT consistently outperform simple test-time scaling and shows limited generalization, raising questions about its effectiveness.
Harness-only improvement hits a 'scaffolding ceiling' when the model lacks reasoning capacity; HarnessX interleaves harness-evolution + model-training (shared replay, cross-harness GRPO) to break it.

AIDE² is claimed first net-positive RSI: 7 successive self-improved versions in 8 days; outer loop cut reward hacking 63%→34% on a held-out GPU-kernel benchmark and beat a human-tuning baseline in 8 days.
The Darwin Gödel Machine iteratively rewrites its own code and improves coding-benchmark performance via open-ended archive evolution (keep-if-interestingly-new).
Curated skills substantially improve success but self-generated skills may DEGRADE it; self-feedback alone induces recursive drift — genuine gains need external feedback across iterations.
Across 17 models the dominant predictor of long-horizon success is persistence in the benchmark→edit→incorporate-feedback loop, not initial-attempt quality; most models quit early.
A stronger search architecture (diversity archive + mutation router + rank-preserving proxy) can substitute for a larger LLM — matches ShinkaEvolve/GEPA at 3.3–35× lower cost with a small model.

LeJEPA can recover the true hidden variables behind raw observations (linear identifiability) under Gaussian latents + stationary additive-noise dynamics; but a formal benchmark finds current world models brittle.
Sora and V-JEPA have NOT learned a complete real-world model (philosophical + benchmark critique): current world models are brittle.
